prompt: Many children now use tablets and computers in the classroom from a very young age. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

plan.intro: Paraphrase and give a clear opinion: advantages outweigh disadvantages (with conditions).
plan.body1: Advantages: interactive and engaging, access to information, digital skills for future jobs, personalised learning speed.
plan.body2: Disadvantages: distraction, less handwriting and face-to-face interaction, screen time and eyesight, cost and inequality. Show that these can be managed.

modelAnswer:
Digital devices have become a common sight in primary classrooms around the world. Although this trend has certain drawbacks, I believe that its benefits are greater, provided that the technology is used sensibly.

The main advantage of tablets and computers is that they make lessons more engaging. Young children often find it difficult to concentrate on textbooks, but educational games, videos and interactive exercises can capture their attention and make abstract subjects, such as mathematics, easier to grasp. Devices also give pupils instant access to a wide range of information, and software can adapt to each child's level, allowing slower learners to practise as long as they need while faster ones move ahead. Moreover, since almost every modern job requires digital skills, children who start early are better prepared for the future.

On the other hand, there are legitimate concerns. Pupils may be distracted by games or messages instead of concentrating on their work, and too much time in front of a screen can harm eyesight and reduce physical activity. Some teachers also worry that children who type most of the time may lose the ability to write neatly by hand and may have fewer opportunities to talk face to face. In addition, buying devices is expensive, which may widen the gap between rich and poor schools.

Nevertheless, I believe these problems can be controlled. Schools can limit screen time, ban non-educational applications and make sure that children still spend part of the day writing, reading real books and working in groups. Governments could also fund equipment for schools in poorer areas.

In conclusion, although digital devices carry some risks, their power to motivate pupils, personalise learning and teach valuable skills means that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages if teachers manage their use carefully.
